errors.english: the reality of union
errors.why: འབྱོར་བ is endowment/accomplishment (sampad), and the next side treats this reality as the supreme siddhi; it is not 'union' (sbyor ba / rnal 'byor).

note: A faithful, readable rendering of the three-realities commentary; only the second reality's name is doubtful.

errors.english: The apprehended does not assist the mind as something not apprehended through a causal chain; since it is impossible to assist without doing so directly, the mind that produces is itself the apprehended.
errors.why: The Tibetan says that indirectly something can assist cognition without being apprehended, but directly assisting without being apprehended is impossible, so what produces the cognition is the apprehended.

fix.find: The apprehended does not assist the mind as something not apprehended through a causal chain; since it is impossible to assist without doing so directly, the mind that produces is itself the apprehended.
fix.replace: Indirectly, something may assist the mind without being apprehended, but directly it is impossible to assist without being apprehended; therefore what produces the cognition is itself the apprehended.

errors.english: An appearance is never anything other than the apprehended;
errors.why: སྣང་བ here is light (āloka), the stock example of a cause of visual cognition alleged not to be its object; the verse says 'it is not that light is not apprehended', and 'appearance' misleads throughout the passage.

fix.find: An appearance is never anything other than the apprehended;
fix.replace: It is not that light is not apprehended;

errors.english: The definition of the producer is nothing other than this.
errors.why: The verse makes being-a-producer the definition of being apprehended (as the commentary then says), not the other way round.

errors.english:
Without being like form and so forth,
There is no direct benefit to the mind.
errors.why: The verse says that form and the like do not directly benefit cognition without being thus (apprehended); form is the subject, not a standard of comparison.

errors.english: For the (samskara) mental formation/conditioning to remain stable, it cannot be determined by anything else.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the saṃskāra merely persists, so the ascertainment does not come from it; the English inverts the dependence.

note: The Pramāṇa argument about the definition of the apprehended is repeatedly garbled, including one reversal and a mistranslated key term (light).

errors.english: the remainderless state [note: referring to nirvana with remainder]
errors.why: The two results are nirvāṇa with and without remainder; calling the first 'remainderless' while glossing it as 'with remainder' is self-contradictory and misleading.

note: A sound rendering of the purpose-and-connection preamble to the Bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa commentary.

errors.english: one satisfies the (Bodhisattvas) beings dedicated to awakening in each and every moment
errors.why: ལྷན་ཅིག means 'together with': the enjoyment body is satisfied moment by moment together with the bodhisattvas, it does not satisfy them.

fix.find: one satisfies the (Bodhisattvas) beings dedicated to awakening in each and every moment
fix.replace: one is satisfied, together with the (Bodhisattvas) beings dedicated to awakening, in each and every moment

errors.english: just as mentioning "Vajrabhairava" allows one to know the entire class of Bhairava deities
errors.why: This is the grammarians' stock example of a part of a name standing for the whole: saying 'Bhīma' one understands Bhīmasena (འཇིགས་བྱེད་ཀྱི་སྡེ), not a class of Bhairava deities.

fix.find: just as mentioning "Vajrabhairava" allows one to know the entire class of Bhairava deities
fix.replace: just as on hearing "Bhīma" one understands Bhīmasena

errors.english: Because it moves everywhere through the application of inspired energy
errors.why: སྤྲོ་བ here is emanating (spharaṇa): it goes everywhere by the practice of emanation, not 'inspired energy'.

note: Generally follows the commentary on the enjoyment and emanation bodies, but misreads who is satisfied and the Bhīma/Bhīmasena example.

errors.english: If that novice dies
errors.why: The Tibetan has དགེ་སློང་, a fully ordained monk, not a novice (dge tshul).

errors.english: If a monk steals those goods from a separate building and moves them
errors.why: The monk steals the goods dedicated to one dwelling and moves them to a separate dwelling; the direction is reversed.

note: Usable rendering of a dense Vinaya commentary on theft valuation and deceased monks' shares; the inline 'original:' tags are clutter rather than errors.
A faithful, polished rendering of the nidāna commentary ('Thus have I heard', bhagavat, the four dwellings); the opening sentences translate the previous side.

errors.english: Harmful actions toward the Three Jewels should be eliminated
errors.why: The verse says those who harm the Three Jewels are to be killed; the English turns the persons into 'actions' and softens the verb, with a note that reinterprets rather than translates.

errors.english: as the disciple becomes a (Tathagata) Thus-Gone One/Buddha
errors.why: It is the officiating master who, having become (identified as) the Tathāgata, gives the prediction; the disciple is not named.

note: A reasonable rendering of the consecration and prediction verses, with two doubtful attributions of agent.

errors.english: which possesses inconceivable worldly abundance
errors.why: Nāgārjuna's verse says the enjoyment body's own splendour transcends the world (lokottara) and is inconceivable, not that it is worldly.

fix.replace: whose own splendour is inconceivable and transcends the world

errors.english: unless they look into the mirror of karma and such
errors.why: The Śakras themselves ascertain, by looking into the mirror of karma, whether the same one or another is reborn, unknown to others; it is not an exception for the ordinary gods.

note: Sound on the debate about whether the enjoyment body passes into nirvāṇa, but the Nāgārjuna verse is reversed on a key point; heavy inline glosses clutter it.

errors.english: even if the objective reality is not as described
errors.why: The clause (begun on the previous side with ཡོད་) says that even though the fact does exist, speaking against one's perception is lying; the contrast with the next sentence ('even though it does not exist') is lost.

fix.find: even if the objective reality is not as described
fix.replace: even if the objective fact does exist

errors.english: This is not because both truth and falsehood are connected to perception, rather than being connected to the objective reality of the matter.
errors.why: The Tibetan gives this as the reason: truth and falsehood are tied to perception, not to the objective fact.

fix.find: This is not because both truth and falsehood are connected to perception, rather than being connected to the objective reality of the matter.
fix.replace: This is because truth and falsehood are tied to perception, not to the objective reality of the matter.

errors.english: against one who is pure
errors.why: མ་དག་པ means impure: the point is that even accusing a monk who really has fallen, on a false basis, incurs the offence (cf. 'even for a fallen monk' below).

fix.replace: against one who is impure (who has in fact fallen)

errors.english: (Sanghadisesa)
errors.why: This is the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya; the Sanskrit term is saṅghāvaśeṣa, not the Pali saṅghādisesa.

note: The argument that lying depends on perception rather than fact is reversed twice, and the fallen/pure monk is inverted; needs a specialist pass.

errors.english: through its simultaneous existence with physical objects
errors.why: The first co-existent (begun on the previous side) is the active consciousnesses (འཇུག་པའི་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པ་དང་ལྷན་ཅིག), and the sentence establishes the ālaya's operation (འཇུག་པ), not physical objects.

note: A faithful rendering of the ālaya-as-root-of-saṃkleśa passage; only the boundary sentence is misread.
